1.note: Isaiah is speaking as if the Spirit of Yahweh were something that could rest physically **on** him. He means that Yahweh’s Spirit is present with him and empowers him for this work. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The Spirit of the Lord Yahweh is present with me and empowers me]

Isaiah is speaking as if Yahweh had **anointed** him by pouring oil on him. In that culture, pouring oil on a person set that person apart for a special task, so here it means that Yahweh has chosen and appointed him for this work. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh has set me apart]

Isaiah is using the adjective **poor** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [to poor people]

The expression **the broken of heart** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [those who have broken hearts]

Isaiah is speaking as if grieving people were injured people whose wounds he could **bind up**. He means that he will comfort and restore those who are suffering deep sorrow. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to comfort those who are grieving deeply]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **freedom**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [that they are now free]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **liberation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [that they are liberated]

Isaiah is using the adjective **bound** as a noun to mean people who are bound. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [and liberation to those who are bound]

2.q: שְׁנַת רָצוֹן֙ לַֽ⁠יהוָ֔ה וְ⁠י֥וֹם נָקָ֖ם לֵ⁠אלֹהֵ֑י⁠נוּ
2.note: Isaiah is using the terms **year** and **day** as common expressions of the culture to mean “an appointed time.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the appointed time of favor of Yahweh, and the appointed time of vengeance of our God]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **vengeance**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [when our God avenges his people]

3.note: Here, **Zion** represents “the people who live there.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [for the mourners among the people of Jerusalem]

The implication is that people would put **ashes** on themselves as a sign of mourning, so giving them **a headdress** instead of ashes signifies that their mourning has turned to joy. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [a headdress to them instead of the ashes they wore while mourning]

Here, **oil** represents festive gladness, since people would anoint themselves with oil at joyful celebrations. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [joyful celebration]

Isaiah is speaking as if praise were a **garment** that a person could put on. He means that the people will be characterized by praise instead of despair. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a disposition of praise]

Here, **spirit** represents “a person’s inner disposition,” in this case one of despair. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [a disposition of despair]

The expression **one will call to them** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And people will call them]

3.q: וְ⁠קֹרָ֤א לָ⁠הֶם֙ & אֵילֵ֣י הַ⁠צֶּ֔דֶק מַטַּ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה לְ⁠הִתְפָּאֵֽר
3.note: The implication is that people will recognize that Yahweh himself made his people righteous and strong, like flourishing oak trees that he planted, and that people will praise him because of this. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And people will call them “oaks of righteousness,” trees that Yahweh planted, so that people will praise him for it]

4.note: The pronoun **they** refers to the people whom Yahweh has restored, spoken of in the previous verses. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the restored people will build]

Isaiah is using **generation and generation** as a common expression of the culture to mean “many successive generations.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [devastations of many generations]

5.note: Isaiah is using **sons of foreignness** as a common expression of the culture to mean “foreigners.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and people from other lands]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **foreignness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [sons of foreign nations]
The words **you** and **your** are plural here and in the next two verses because Isaiah is addressing the Israelites, so use plural forms in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

6.note: The expression **you will be called** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [people will call you priests of Yahweh]

Isaiah is repeating the word **you** in order to emphasize and intensify the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [And you yourselves will be called priests of Yahweh]

Isaiah is speaking as if the people were literally **priests of Yahweh**. He means that they will have a special, honored relationship with Yahweh and will serve him as priests did. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [people who serve Yahweh in a special, honored way]

The expression **will be said to you** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [is what people will call you]

Isaiah is speaking as if the people would literally **eat** the wealth of other nations. He means that they will consume and enjoy those valuable things. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You will enjoy the wealth of nations]

Here, **glory** represents “the wealth of the nations.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and you will boast yourself in their wealth]

7.note: Isaiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [Instead of your shame, they will have double]

Even though Isaiah is addressing his people directly, he speaks of them in the third person as **they** and **their**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the second person. Alternate translation: [you will shout over your portion. Therefore, in your land you will possess double; eternal joy will be yours]

8.note: The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [This is because]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **justice**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what is just]

The implication is that Yahweh hates it when people present to him offerings that they themselves obtained by robbing others. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [hating it when someone offers stolen goods to me]

The phrase translated as **in burnt offering** represents the standard Hebrew text as we have it today. Scholars have noted that with different vowels supplied to the original consonants, the phrase would be “with injustice.” That would provide a closer parallel to the preceding line. The UST follows that interpretation. You may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [robbery with injustice]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **truth**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [faithfully]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **eternity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [I will cut a covenant that will last forever for them]

Yahweh is using **cut a covenant** as a common expression of the culture to mean “to make a covenant.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I will make an eternal covenant with them]

9.note: The expression **their seed will be known** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And people will know their seed]

Yahweh is speaking as if the people’s descendants were **seed** that had been planted and grown. He means their offspring and those who come after them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [their offspring]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and their offspring will be known in the midst of the peoples]

10.note: Isaiah is repeating forms of the verb **rejoice** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [I will greatly rejoice]

Isaiah is using **my soul** to represent his whole self. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I myself]

10.q: הִלְבִּישַׁ֨⁠נִי֙ בִּגְדֵי יֶ֔שַׁע מְעִ֥יל צְדָקָ֖ה יְעָטָ֑⁠נִי
10.note: Isaiah is speaking as if salvation and righteousness were **garments** and a **robe** that Yahweh had put on him. He means that Yahweh has saved him and made him righteous. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he has saved me; he has made me righteous]

10.q: כֶּֽ⁠חָתָן֙ יְכַהֵ֣ן פְּאֵ֔ר וְ⁠כַ⁠כַּלָּ֖ה תַּעְדֶּ֥ה כֵלֶֽי⁠הָ
10.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **a bridegroom** and **a bride** make themselves beautiful with fine adornments, so Yahweh has made Isaiah beautiful by clothing him with salvation and righteousness. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [just as a bridegroom makes himself beautiful with a headdress, and just as a bride makes herself beautiful with her jewels, so he has made me beautiful]

11.q: כָ⁠אָ֨רֶץ֙ תּוֹצִ֣יא צִמְחָ֔⁠הּ וּ⁠כְ⁠גַנָּ֖ה זֵרוּעֶ֣י⁠הָ תַצְמִ֑יחַ כֵּ֣ן אֲדֹנָ֣⁠י יְהוִ֗ה יַצְמִ֤יחַ צְדָקָה֙ וּ⁠תְהִלָּ֔ה
11.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **the earth** and **a garden** cause plants to sprout and grow, so the Lord Yahweh will surely cause righteousness and praise to spring up before all the nations. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [just as surely as the earth produces plants and a garden produces growth from the seeds sown in it, the Lord Yahweh will just as surely produce righteousness and praise]
